notes: Method: one pass per folder, reading each folder's .md files with shell cat/grep. Instruction counts (n_instructions_estimate) are rough; for the large UI-canon folder (IntrustIT, ~100k words) the 400 is a guess. Folders over or near 30k words (IntrustIT, sonic-mast, RDForward, ruflo-patch, vani-compiler) had reference/protocol notes skimmed by grepping for directives (never/always/must/commit/push/delete/etc.) and reading hits in context. A file-level clash hidden in prose without those keywords could be missed there. summoner-build-lab's two skill catalogs were also skimmed even though that folder is small. file_instructions lists the clearer file-action instructions, not every one. Code-style rules (e.g. 'put components in X') were included when they name a path. Rules about the content of commit messages (no Co-Authored-By) were left out of file_instructions as not file actions, but are noted in other_topics. A rule that names several paths appears as one entry with a combined target. 'settled' was used when a later dated note or an explicit SUPERSEDED/exception marker exists, even when the older file was not updated; most of those are marked unsure. Several 'clashes' are a stale fact (jar version, domain, env path) against a current instruction; their topic was set honestly but they may not count as instruction clashes under a strict reading. Pensieve's CLAUDE.md holds just the text 'AGENTS.md' (AGENTS.md is not a .md in scope). intrust-canon's feedback refers to a MEMORY.md that does not exist in that folder.
